_about: Scope decisions for .claude/skills/bollywood-actor-filmography/scripts/extract_wiki.py films. Not read by build_workbook.py.

exclude.Anusandhan|1981: Bengali version of the bilingual Barsaat Ki Ek Raat; both titles lead to one Wikipedia article, so the film has one master row.
exclude.Zamaanat|2006: Listed in the filmography as unreleased.
exclude.Veergatha|2016: No Wikipedia article or citation; IMDb describes an audiovisual on twelve Param Vir Chakra recipients, with no evidence of a theatrical feature release.
exclude.Bunty Aur Babli 2|2021: Archival footage only; no new performance.

notes.Barsaat Ki Ek Raat|1981: Bilingual production shot simultaneously in Hindi and Bengali; the Bengali version, Anusandhan, has no separate row. The Wikipedia article is titled Anusandhan (1981 film).
notes.Kaasdaya Kandane|1974: No Wikipedia article; the filmography cites a Hindustan Times article on Tulu cinema for the voiceover.
notes.Film Hi Film|1983: No Wikipedia article and no citation in the filmography; IMDb credits Bachchan as Jengo / Guru and marks much of the cast as archive footage.
notes.Kanoon Kya Karega|1984: No Wikipedia article and no citation in the filmography; IMDb credits Bachchan as narrator.
notes.Pet Pyaar Aur Paap|1984: No Wikipedia article and no citation in the filmography; IMDb credits him as himself in a guest appearance.
notes.Akka|1994: No Wikipedia article; the filmography cites a Firstpost video page for the guest appearance.
notes.Ahsaas|1979: No film article; the title redirects to List of Hindi films of 1979.
notes.Ek Krantiveer: Vasudev Balwant Phadke|20: No Wikipedia article and no citation in the filmography; IMDb lists Bachchan as narrator.
notes.Ganga Devi|2012: No Wikipedia article; the filmography cites a Times of India music-launch report.
notes.The Great Leader|2017: No Wikipedia article and no citation in the filmography; IMDb lists a 2017 release. Reported as a Bhojpuri film dubbed in Hindi, produced by his long-time make-up artist Deepak Sawant.
notes.Bombay Talkie|1970: Uncredited. The film article lists him as a man attending a funeral and also reports his account that he left after one day of shooting, before he was due to deliver his line; the filmography cites only a MensXP list.
notes.The Ghazi Attack|2017: The infobox language field reads Telugu, then Tamil and Hindi on one line; entered as three languages.
notes.Guddi|1971: The film article lists Amitabh Bachchan among actors who make guest appearances as themselves.
